description: Execution-cost model: TAKER (market) vs POST-ONLY LIMIT (maker). Breakeven fill-rate + per-book Sharpe impact. RESEARCH ONLY — all maker params are swept assumptions.

cost_decomposition.note: 8.5 = 3.5 taker fee + 5.0 implied slippage; maker fee 1.0bps base tier, NO rebate

maker_model.policy_A: cross-after-timeout: unfilled portion crosses as taker
maker_model.policy_B: skip/tracking-error: unfilled portion stays off target book (qualitative)

breakeven.interpretation: fill-rate at which policy-A E[cost] == 8.5bps taker; above p* maker saves, below p* maker is worse

policy_B_tracking_error_bound.p0.3: book holds 70% less of intended rebal delta/period
policy_B_tracking_error_bound.p0.5: book holds 50% less of intended rebal delta/period
policy_B_tracking_error_bound.p0.7: book holds 30% less of intended rebal delta/period
policy_B_tracking_error_bound.p0.9: book holds 10% less of intended rebal delta/period
policy_B_tracking_error_bound.p1.0: book holds 0% less of intended rebal delta/period

caveats: NO order-book / spread data and NO measured fill-rate in this research panel. spread_capture, adverse_selection, drift_penalty and p_fill are ASSUMPTIONS, sensitivity-swept here, NOT measured.

Real fill-rate + spread must come from (a) auditing the live prod fills DB and (b) a live post-only A/B test. This model frames 'what fill-rate is needed and what is at stake' — it does NOT prove maker is cheaper.
HL maker fee 1.0 bps is BASE TIER. No rebate is assumed (rebates need volume our ~$345 occupied capital does not generate).
Policy B (skip) is tracking error, not a per-leg bp cost; quantitative results are policy A (cross-after-timeout) only. B is a documented caveat.

Maker changes are LIVE EXECUTION changes to src/frab — OUT OF SCOPE here (research only). Adverse selection is hardest on thin alts (wide spread, low fill-rate) and on a directional book that chases momentum.
Turnover is measured on the PT survivorship panel; live universe (~15-20 coins) and live rebalance cadence may differ from the backtest grid.
verdict: MAKER SWITCH — CONDITIONALLY worth pursuing, and it matters MOST for the TREND book by a wide margin. Decomposition: research 8.5bps/leg = 3.5 taker fee + 5.0 implied slippage; HL maker fee is 1.0bps. At default params (spread_capture 2.5, adverse_selection 2.5, drift 1.5) the breakeven is p_fill*=0.17: we must fill >=17% of legs passively for maker (policy A) to beat all-taker. The stakes scale with turnover: TREND (~236/yr) is ~4.3x more cost-sensitive than XSMOM (~54/yr), so the same per-bp saving buys ~4.3x more Sharpe/return on TREND. At effective 3bps vs 8.5, TREND gains Sharpe +0.083 (ann +12.95pp) vs XSMOM +0.077 (ann +2.99pp). PLAUSIBILITY: a weekly target-book reconcile on liquid majors can plausibly fill >=17% passively; thin alts (wide spread → biggest fee win) are exactly where fill-risk + adverse selection are worst, so a blended fill-rate near breakeven is realistic but UNCERTAIN. DECISION: do NOT flip live blindly. First audit the live prod fills DB for realized spread + passive fill-rate, then run a live post-only A/B test — prioritising TREND, where the per-bp payoff is largest.
